Coram :
Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha

Oral Judgment
1. Heard the arguments of both sides.
2.  This appeal is filed against the judgment and award of the Tribunal in MVC No.376/2022 dated 16.01.2025.
Injured claimant met with an accident on 02.01.2022 and filed claim petition claiming compensation of 27,00,000/-.
The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of  11,07,993/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
Aggrieved by the said order, preferred the present appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC:6663 HC-KAR Counsel for the appellant mainly contended that he was admitted as an inpatient for nine days.
He sustained grievous injuries.
He spent  5,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
But, the Tribunal granted only  3,34,693/-.
He also examined the doctor as PW2 and doctor assessed the disability as 62.31% to the right lower limb and 31.15% to the whole body.

But,
the Tribunal granted only 20%.
He was working as a owner cum driver and earning  30,000/- per month.
He was aged 42 years.
But Tribunal has taken notional income of  15,500/- and the amounts granted under the other heads is bigger.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation and also rate of interest.
3. Though petitioner stated that he was earning  30,000/- he has not filed any income proof.

As he met with an accident in the year 2022, the Tribunal has rightly considered his income as  15,500/-
and it needs no interference.
He was aged 42 years and the multiplier is 14.

The petitioner also examined doctor as PW2 and he stated as follows;
"(1) right acetabulum posterior wall open reduction and internal fixation with plate and screw done on 4-1-2022.
(2) right acetabulum anterior wall closed reduction and internal fixation with cannulated cancellous screw was done on 7-1-2022 and discharged on 11-1-2022."
6.
assessed the permanent residual physical disability of about 62.31% of right lower limb and right hemi pelvis which about 31.15% of wholebody.
PW-2 produced Ex-P14 OPD slip, Ex-P15-x-rays."
7. It is stated that he is not a treated doctor.
The Tribunal has considered the functional disability as 20%.

The evidence of PW2 shows that there is malunion of anterior column fracture of right acetabulum and so also, fracture of right fibula upper aspect shows malunion and right hip joint necessitating a total hip joint replacement in near future and it was also suggested that he needs hip joint replacement.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 21%.
Hence, loss of future income comes NC: 2026:KHC:6663 HC-KAR to  15,500/- x 12 x 14 x 21% =  6,83,550/-
This Court finds that the amounts granted by the Tribunal under other heads are just and reasonable and it needs no interference.

9. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:

 1. Pain and suffering 1,00,000/-
 2. Loss of amenities' 50,000/-

 nourishment charges

 5. Loss of income during laid up 77,500/-
 period  6.

Medical expenses 3,34,693/-
 7.

Future medical expenses 75,000/-
 Total 13,50,743/-
NC: 2026:KHC:6663 HC-KAR 10.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.11,07,993/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.13,50,743/-.
Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,42,750/- (Rs.13,50,743/- - Rs.11,07,993/-).
11. Respondent No.1 has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal.

Hence,
respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,42,750/- before the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
12.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 16.01.32025 passed in M.V.C.No.376/2022 by the IV Additional Judge and MACT and ACJM, Bengaluru (SCCH-6), is hereby modified holding that the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,42,750/- along NC: 2026:KHC:6663 HC-KAR with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
